title.zh: 卷384 列傳一百七十一 林培厚 李象鶤 李宗傳 王凤生 黄冕 兪德渊 姚莹
title.en: Volume 384 Biographies 171: Lin Peihou, Li Xiangkun, Li Zongchuan, Wang Fengsheng, Huang Mian, Yu De Yuan, Yao Ying
title.raw: 卷384 列傳一百七十一 林培厚 李象鶤 李宗傳 王凤生 黄冕 兪德渊 姚莹

sentences.zh: 林培厚，字敏齋，浙江瑞安人。

translations.literal: Lin Peihou, courtesy name Minzhai, was a native of Ruian, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Peihou, whose courtesy name was Minzhai, came from Ruian in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of the Jiaqing reign he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor in the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in Jiaqing 13, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and received an appointment as compiler.

sentences.zh: 出為四川重慶知府。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as prefect of Chongqing in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was then posted as prefect of Chongqing in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 啯匪帶刀異常制，禁鍛者毋制賣，有犯則坐。

translations.literal: Bandits carrying knives violated the usual regulations; he forbade smiths to sell regulated blades, and offenders were prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Local bandits had taken to carrying knives in defiance of the rules, so he barred armorers from selling regulated blades and prosecuted anyone who violated the ban.

sentences.zh: 沿江渡船為盜資，籍而稽其出入，刻姓名船側，盜為衰息。

translations.literal: Ferry boats along the river supplied robbers; he registered them and checked their comings and goings, carving names on the sides of boats, and banditry declined.
translations.idiomatic: River ferries were feeding the robbers, so he registered every boat, tracked traffic in and out, and had owners’ names carved on the hulls; banditry soon waned.

sentences.zh: 民習天主教，搜其書，批抉繆妄，聞者多悔悟。

translations.literal: The people practiced Catholicism; he searched out their books, refuted their errors, and many who heard him repented.
translations.idiomatic: Catholicism had taken root among the people; he seized their books, exposed their fallacies, and many listeners came to repent.

sentences.zh: 署川東道，所屬雷波廳民、夷忿爭，或覬覦邀功，請發兵，培厚不應，立縛治其魁，餘悉貸遣。

translations.literal: Acting as intendant of eastern Sichuan, when Han and Yi in Leibo subprefecture quarreled and some sought glory by asking for troops, Peihou refused, immediately bound and punished the ringleaders, and pardoned the rest.
translations.idiomatic: While acting intendant of eastern Sichuan, Han and Yi in Leibo subprefecture fell into bitter strife; some officials, eager for credit, urged him to send troops. Peihou refused, seized the ringleaders at once, and released the rest with pardon.

sentences.zh: 總督蔣攸銛器之，稱為蜀中良吏之最。

translations.literal: Governor-General Jiang Youjie valued him and called him the finest official in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Jiang Youjie prized his ability and hailed him as the best magistrate in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，服闋，授直隸天津府。

translations.literal: He returned home on his mother’s mourning; when the mourning ended he was appointed to Zhili’s Tianjin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home for his mother’s mourning, he was appointed prefect of Tianjin in Zhili when the period of grief ended.

sentences.zh: 畿輔大水，天津地窪下，災尤劇，培厚遍行屬縣，賑活饑民七萬有奇。

translations.literal: Great floods struck the capital region; Tianjin, low-lying, suffered worst; Peihou toured every subordinate county and relieved more than seventy thousand starving people.
translations.idiomatic: Floods ravaged the capital region, and low-lying Tianjin suffered worst of all. Peihou toured every county under his jurisdiction and kept more than seventy thousand starving people alive.

sentences.zh: 奉天、台灣商米先後抵海口，議以官錢收買，委曲劑量，商民交利，而官不費。

translations.literal: Merchant rice from Fengtian and Taiwan reached the port in succession; he proposed buying it with official funds, weighing matters carefully, so merchants and people both profited while the government spent nothing.
translations.idiomatic: As merchant grain from Fengtian and Taiwan reached the harbor in turn, he proposed purchasing it with public funds after careful calculation, so traders and townsfolk alike benefited while the treasury spent nothing.

sentences.zh: 時蔣攸銛移督直隸，詔舉賢吏，遂薦之，不旬日，擢大順廣道。

translations.literal: At that time Jiang Youjie had been transferred to govern Zhili; the throne ordered recommendations of worthy officials, and he recommended Peihou; within ten days Peihou was promoted to intendant of Dashunguang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Youjie had by then been moved to govern Zhili; when the court called for worthy officials, he recommended Peihou, who within ten days was promoted intendant of Dashunguang.

sentences.zh: 畿南澇後，大興水利。

translations.literal: After flooding in southern Zhili, great waterworks were undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: After the southern Zhili floods, major hydraulic works were launched.

sentences.zh: 培厚先在天津治淀河，至大名治新衛河、洺河，浚築悉中程度。

translations.literal: Peihou had first worked on the Dian River at Tianjin; at Daming he worked on the Xinwei and Ming rivers, and in dredging and embankment all met the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Peihou had first managed the Dian River at Tianjin; at Daming he took on the Xinwei and Ming rivers, and every dredging and embankment project met specification.

sentences.zh: 培厚數以時事利病、屬吏賢否語攸銛，為布政使屠之申所忌。

translations.literal: Peihou often told Youjie of current benefits and harms and whether subordinates were worthy; this was resented by Provincial Administration Commissioner Tu Zhishen.
translations.idiomatic: Peihou often reported to Youjie on the gains and losses of current policy and on which subordinates were fit for office—reports that Provincial Administration Commissioner Tu Zhishen resented.

sentences.zh: 及攸銛入相，那彥成代之，坐河北旱荒施賑不如法，解培厚任，宣宗夙知其能，改授湖北糧儲道。

translations.literal: When Youjie entered the Grand Council, Nayancheng replaced him; because relief in the Hebei drought had not followed regulations, Peihou was removed; the Xuanzong Emperor had long known his ability and reassigned him intendant of grain transport in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: When Youjie joined the Grand Council, Nayancheng took his place and, citing improper drought relief in Hebei, stripped Peihou of his post; the Xuanzong Emperor, who had long known his talent, reassigned him intendant of grain transport in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 時河患淺涸，漕舟數阻。

translations.literal: At the time the river suffered shallow drought and grain boats were often blocked.
translations.idiomatic: The waterways were then shallow and drought-stricken, and grain transports were repeatedly stalled.

sentences.zh: 攸銛以大學士出督兩江，期八省漕以首夏畢渡河，乘清水盛漲，浮渡遄利。

translations.literal: Youjie went out as Grand Secretary to supervise the Two Jiangs, fixing that grain from eight provinces should finish crossing the river by early summer, riding high clear water for swift passage.
translations.idiomatic: Youjie left the capital as Grand Secretary to oversee the Two Jiangs, setting a deadline for grain from eight provinces to cross the river by early summer, when the clear flood would carry the fleet swiftly through.

sentences.zh: 培厚所部尤速達，為嘉慶以來數十年所未有，攸銛特疏陳給敘。

translations.literal: Peihou’s jurisdiction was especially quick; such speed had not been seen in decades since Jiaqing; Youjie memorialized specially to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: The sector under Peihou moved faster than any other—something not seen in decades since Jiaqing—and Youjie submitted a special memorial recommending him for reward.

sentences.zh: 曆三運無誤，上意方鄉用，以勞卒於通州運次。

translations.literal: Through three transport cycles without error, the court was about to promote him when he died of overwork at Tongzhou during a transport rotation.
translations.idiomatic: After three transport cycles without a hitch, the throne was ready to promote him when he died of exhaustion at Tongzhou during a transport rotation.

sentences.zh: 李象鶤，字云皋，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: Li Xiangkun, courtesy name Yunguo, was a native of Changsha, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiangkun, whose courtesy name was Yunguo, was from Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Jiaqing 16, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，出為直隸宣化知府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he went out as prefect of Xuanhua in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 2 he was posted prefect of Xuanhua in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，禁姦販，安屯戶，煮粥以賑，民無失所。

translations.literal: In a famine year he banned profiteering, settled garrison households, and gave gruel relief so the people did not wander homeless.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine he banned hoarding and profiteering, settled garrison households, and distributed congee relief so no one was left destitute.

sentences.zh: 課士有法，一變邊郡弇陋之習。

translations.literal: He had method in examining scholars and changed the crude habits of the frontier commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His examinations of scholars were rigorous, and he transformed the backward habits of that frontier prefecture.

sentences.zh: 調正定，再調保定。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zhengding, then again to Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Zhengding and later to Baoding.

sentences.zh: 蔣攸銛、那彥成先後為總督，皆倚如左右手。

translations.literal: Jiang Youjie and Nayancheng served as governor-general in succession, both relying on him as on right and left hands.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Youjie and Nayancheng, serving as governor-general in turn, both leaned on him as they would on their own hands.

sentences.zh: 象鶤持正無撓，擢通永道，調河南鹽道。

translations.literal: Xiangkun was upright and unyielding; he was promoted intendant of Tongyong, then transferred intendant of salt in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangkun stood firm and would not bend; he rose to intendant of Tongyong and was then moved to the Henan salt intendant.

sentences.zh: 治漕嚴，弁丁懍懍，禁胥役藉僱剝船擾民，請潞鹽仍歸商運，民便之。

translations.literal: He was strict in managing transport; boatmen were in awe; he forbade clerks and runners from hiring boats to extort the people; he asked that Lu salt return to merchant transport, to the people’s convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He ran the grain transport with iron discipline, cowing the boatmen; he barred clerks and runners from hiring boats to harass the people; and he petitioned that Lu salt revert to merchant carriage, which eased life for the populace.

sentences.zh: 丁父艱歸，服闋，補江西吉南贛寧道。

translations.literal: He returned on his father’s mourning; when mourning ended he was appointed intendant of Jinan-Gan-Ning in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for his father’s mourning; when the period ended he was named intendant of Jinan-Gan-Ning in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 轄境與粵東犬牙相錯，多伏莽，屬縣僻瘠，幾不可治，象鶤掃除積弊，境內秩然。

translations.literal: His jurisdiction interlocked with eastern Guangdong, with many hidden strongholds; subordinate counties were remote and poor, nearly ungovernable; Xiangkun swept away accumulated abuses and the territory became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: His territory meshed with eastern Guangdong, with many hidden lairs; subordinate counties were remote and impoverished, almost beyond rule. Xiangkun cleared out long-standing abuses until the region was orderly again.

sentences.zh: 擢江蘇按察使，署江寧布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted provincial judicial commissioner of Jiangsu and acted as Jiangning administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted provincial judicial commissioner of Jiangsu and served concurrently as acting administration commissioner of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 時陶澍為總督，賴其佐理焉。

translations.literal: At the time Tao Shu was governor-general and relied on him to assist in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Tao Shu then relied on him to help run the province.

sentences.zh: 調貴州按察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred provincial judicial commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as provincial judicial commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 仁懷奸民為亂，株連眾，治之無枉縱。

translations.literal: Wicked men in Renhuai made trouble; many were implicated; he judged without wrongful leniency or harshness.
translations.idiomatic: When villains in Renhuai stirred up trouble and implicated a crowd of people, he tried the case without either wrongful leniency or undue severity.

sentences.zh: 擢布政使，禁漢奸盤剝苗民，多惠政。

translations.literal: Promoted administration commissioner, he forbade Han traitors from exploiting the Miao and enacted many benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to administration commissioner, he barred Han collaborators from squeezing the Miao and put many humane policies into effect.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以假去職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he left office on leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he left office on personal leave.

sentences.zh: 洎入覲，詔以三品京堂候補。

translations.literal: When he came to court on audience, he was ordered to await appointment as capital official of third rank.
translations.idiomatic: When he later presented himself at court, he was ordered to await appointment as a third-rank capital official.

sentences.zh: 未幾，乞歸。

translations.literal: Before long he asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 李宗傳，字孝曾，安徽桐城人。

translations.literal: Li Zongchuan, courtesy name Xiaozeng, was a native of Tongcheng, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongchuan, whose courtesy name was Xiaozeng, came from Tongcheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶三年舉人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in Jiaqing 3.

sentences.zh: 授浙江上虞知縣先攝麗水、平湖、瑞安、建德、平陽，所至求民隱，鋤豪強，平反冤獄。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Shangyu in Zhejiang, he first acted for Lishui, Pinghu, Ruian, Jiande, and Pingyang; wherever he went he sought the people’s hidden grievances, cut down powerful families, and reversed unjust cases.
translations.idiomatic: Named magistrate of Shangyu in Zhejiang, he first served in acting posts at Lishui, Pinghu, Ruian, Jiande, and Pingyang; everywhere he went he sought out hidden grievances, broke powerful lineages, and reversed wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 在麗水斷積案七百餘事，捐貲河工，敘知府，擢浙江督糧道。

translations.literal: At Lishui he closed more than seven hundred accumulated cases, donated funds for river works, was commended for promotion to prefect, and was raised intendant of grain transport in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: At Lishui he cleared more than seven hundred backlog cases, donated funds for river works, earned commendation toward promotion as prefect, and was raised to Zhejiang’s grain transport intendant.

sentences.zh: 道光三年，杭、嘉、湖三府大水，宗傳建議，浙西諸水尾閭，下由江蘇入海，必宜江、浙兩省通籌疏濬，大吏用其言，疏請合治。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang great floods struck Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou; Zongchuan proposed that the western Zhejiang waterways, whose lower reaches entered the sea through Jiangsu, must be dredged jointly by the two provinces; the high officials adopted his view and memorialized for joint treatment.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 3 floods inundated Hangzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou. Zongchuan argued that the western Zhejiang rivers, whose lower reaches reached the sea through Jiangsu, had to be dredged in concert by both provinces; senior officials took his advice and memorialized for joint works.

sentences.zh: 坐事左遷，巡撫程含章薦之，以知府用，授湖南永州，葺濂溪書院，崇節義，勸種植。

translations.literal: Demoted for an offense, he was recommended by Governor Fu Chengzhang and employed as prefect, appointed to Yongzhou in Hunan, where he repaired the Lianxi Academy, honored integrity, and encouraged planting.
translations.idiomatic: After a demotion, Governor Chengzhang recommended him for use as prefect and sent him to Yongzhou in Hunan, where he restored the Lianxi Academy, exalted righteous conduct, and urged the people to plant trees.

sentences.zh: 擢四川成綿龍茂道，累攝鹽道、布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted intendant of Cheng-Mian-Long-Mao in Sichuan and repeatedly acted as salt intendant and administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted intendant of Cheng-Mian-Long-Mao in Sichuan and repeatedly served as acting salt intendant and administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十三年，瓘邊屬倮夷降复叛，勢甚張，總督鄂山既奏劾提督楊芳，檄宗傳往察治。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Luo Yi of the border of Yunnan submitted then rebelled again with great force; Governor-General E Shan had already memorialized to impeach Regional Commander Yang Fang and ordered Zongchuan to go investigate and settle matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Luo Yi on the Yunnan frontier submitted, then rebelled again in force. Governor-General E Shan had already impeached Regional Commander Yang Fang and ordered Zongchuan to go inspect and settle the affair.

sentences.zh: 宗傳上言：「四廳夷環山為巢，嗜利頑鈍，愈撫愈囂。

translations.literal: Zongchuan memorialized: “The Yi of the four subprefectures nest in mountains all around; greedy and stubborn, the more they are appeased the more arrogant they grow.
translations.idiomatic: Zongchuan wrote: “The Yi of the four subprefectures nest in encircling mountains; greedy and obstinate, they grow bolder the more they are placated.

sentences.zh: 去年添兵設防，夷轉四出焚掠，攻壘窺城，略無忌憚。

translations.literal: Last year troops were added for defense, yet the Yi ranged out on all sides burning and plundering, attacking stockades and watching the cities, with scarcely any restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Last year more troops were posted in defense, yet the Yi ranged out on all sides, burning and looting, assaulting stockades and probing the cities, with almost no restraint.

sentences.zh: 雖擾一廳，實四廳安危所繫，不可姑息貽患。

translations.literal: Though they disturb one subprefecture, the safety of all four is involved; one cannot indulge them and leave future trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Though they harass one subprefecture, the safety of all four hangs on this; indulgence now will breed disaster later.

sentences.zh: 」乃建三路進剿之策，倡助軍需，治兵選士，聲威大振。

translations.literal: ” He then devised a three-route campaign, urged military supplies, trained soldiers and selected officers, and his prestige rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: ” He then planned a three-pronged campaign, rallied military supplies, drilled troops and picked officers, and his prestige soared.

sentences.zh: 三路大軍猶未至，宗傳先以計誘降十三支夷，縶之，勒還所掠人口，有業者復之，無業者給貲，縱俘歸，使諭威德。

translations.literal: Before the three armies arrived, Zongchuan first by stratagem induced thirteen Yi bands to surrender, bound them, forced return of captives, restored those with livelihoods, gave money to those without, released prisoners to announce favor and awe.
translations.idiomatic: Before the three armies arrived, Zongchuan by stratagem induced thirteen Yi bands to surrender, seized them, compelled the return of captives, restored those who had property, paid those who had none, and sent prisoners home to proclaim imperial favor and terror.

sentences.zh: 夷猶豫未決，大軍由冷跡關逼老林巢藪，大破之於石門坎，擒斬數百，毀賊寨二百餘所，夷落悉平。

translations.literal: The Yi still hesitated; the main force pressed through Lengji Pass toward the old forest lairs and broke them at Shimenkan, killing and capturing hundreds, destroying more than two hundred bandit camps, and the Yi settlements were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: While the Yi still wavered, the main force pressed through Cold Trace Pass toward the old forest strongholds and routed them at Shimen Ridge, killing and capturing hundreds and destroying more than two hundred rebel camps until every Yi settlement was pacified.

sentences.zh: 論功最，擢山東按察使。

translations.literal: Judged foremost in merit, he was promoted provincial judicial commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Rated first in merit, he was promoted provincial judicial commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 捕大盜劉二鞍子置之法，群盜遠遁，遷湖北布政使。

translations.literal: He captured the great bandit Liu Er’anzi and executed him by law; bandits fled far away; he was moved to administration commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the great outlaw Liu Er’anzi and put him to death; the rest fled far afield; he was transferred to administration commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 年逾七十，引疾歸。

translations.literal: Past seventy, he cited illness and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Past seventy, he pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 宗傳徵叛夷出奇有功，然居恆時以計取傷仁，意不自慊。

translations.literal: Zongchuan had won merit by stratagem against rebellious Yi, yet in ordinary times when he won by scheme he felt he had injured benevolence and was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Zongchuan had won his merit against rebellious Yi by stratagem, yet in ordinary times, when victory came by trickery, he felt he had wounded humaneness and could not be easy in his mind.

sentences.zh: 嘗從同縣姚鼐遊，能文章。

translations.literal: He had studied under Yao Nai of the same county and could write essays.
translations.idiomatic: He had studied under his fellow townsman Yao Nai and could write well.

sentences.zh: 王鳳生，字竹嶼，安徽婺源人。

translations.literal: Wang Fengsheng, courtesy name Zhuyu, was a native of Wuyuan, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fengsheng, whose courtesy name was Zhuyu, came from Wuyuan in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 父友亮，乾隆四十六年進士。

translations.literal: His father Youliang passed the jinshi in the forty-sixth year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Youliang took the jinshi in Qianlong 46.

sentences.zh: 由中書充軍機章京，累遷刑部郎中，精究法律，治獄矜慎。

translations.literal: From central secretary he served as clerk of the Grand Council, rose to director in the Ministry of Punishments, mastered law, and judged cases with caution.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a central secretary, he served as Grand Council clerk, rose to director in the Ministry of Punishments, mastered the statutes, and tried cases with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 改御史，巡城、巡漕，官至通政司副使，有清直聲。

translations.literal: Made censor, he patrolled the capital and grain transport, rose to vice commissioner of the Court of Transmission, and had a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Made censor, he inspected the capital and the grain route, reached vice commissioner of the Court of Transmission, and won a name for upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 以詩名。

translations.literal: He was famed for poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He was also known as a poet.

sentences.zh: 鳳生，嘉慶中，入貲為浙江通判，屢攝知縣事。

translations.literal: Fengsheng, in the Jiaqing period, purchased office as subprefect of Zhejiang and repeatedly acted as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiaqing, Fengsheng bought office as a Zhejiang subprefect and repeatedly acted as county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 任蘭溪僅數月，清積案七百餘事。

translations.literal: At Lanxi for only a few months he cleared more than seven hundred backlog cases.
translations.idiomatic: At Lanxi, in only a few months, he cleared more than seven hundred backlog cases.

sentences.zh: 任平湖，有民數百戶，誦經茹素，傳授邪教，鳳生憫其愚惑，開諭利害，治為首數人罪，餘釋之。

translations.literal: At Pinghu several hundred households chanted sutras, ate vegetables, and transmitted heterodox teachings; Fengsheng pitied their delusion, explained the harm, punished a few leaders, and released the rest.
translations.idiomatic: At Pinghu several hundred households chanted scriptures, ate only vegetables, and spread heterodox teachings. Fengsheng pitied their delusion, explained the harm, punished the ringleaders, and released the rest.

sentences.zh: 補嘉興府通判。

translations.literal: He was appointed subprefect of Jiaxing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed subprefect of Jiaxing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 道光初，浙江清查倉庫，以鳳生總其事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daoguang Zhejiang audited granaries and warehouses, with Fengsheng in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daoguang, Zhejiang audited its granaries and storehouses under Fengsheng’s direction.

sentences.zh: 署嘉興知府，遷玉環廳同知。

translations.literal: He acted as prefect of Jiaxing and was moved subprefect of Yuhuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting prefect of Jiaxing and was transferred subprefect of Yuhuan.

sentences.zh: 會浙西大水，江、浙兩省議合治，調鳳生乍浦同知，勘水道，乃由天目山歷湖州、嘉興，沿太湖以達松江。

translations.literal: When western Zhejiang flooded, Jiangsu and Zhejiang planned joint works; Fengsheng was moved subprefect of Zhapu to survey waterways, from Tianmu Mountain through Huzhou and Jiaxing along Taihu to Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When western Zhejiang flooded and the two provinces planned joint works, Fengsheng was moved to Zhapu subprefect to survey waterways from Tianmu Mountain through Huzhou and Jiaxing along Lake Tai to Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 計畫甫就，事未行，值淮南高堰潰決，江南大吏疏調鳳生赴南河。

translations.literal: The plan was just finished but not yet carried out when the Gaoyan embankment on the Huai burst; southern officials memorialized to transfer Fengsheng to the Southern Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: His plan was barely finished when the Gaoyan embankment on the Huai collapsed; officials in the south memorialized to transfer him to the Southern Rivers.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢河南歸德知府，濬虞城、夏邑、永城三縣溝渠。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted prefect of Guide in Henan and dredged canals in Yucheng, Xiayi, and Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted prefect of Guide in Henan and dredged the canals of Yucheng, Xiayi, and Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 尋擢彰衛懷道，道屬河工五廳，歲修糜費，春秋防汛，虛應故事，鳳生力矯積習，事必躬親。

translations.literal: Soon raised intendant of Zhang-Wei-Huai, whose five river offices yearly wasted funds on maintenance; spring and autumn flood defense was empty form; Fengsheng forcefully corrected old abuses and attended to everything himself.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised intendant of Zhang-Wei-Huai, whose five river offices yearly squandered maintenance funds while spring and autumn flood defense was mere show. Fengsheng forcefully corrected entrenched abuses and oversaw every task in person.

sentences.zh: 以歲修有定例，另案無定例，在任三年，力刪另案以杜弊。

translations.literal: Because yearly repairs had fixed regulations while extra cases had none, in three years in office he strove to cut extra cases to stop abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Routine annual repairs had fixed rules, but “extra” projects did not; in three years he worked to abolish those extras and choke off corruption.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾乞歸。

translations.literal: Soon he begged leave on illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 九年，兩江總督蔣攸銛薦起原官，署兩淮鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Governor-General Jiang Youjie recommended him to his former post, acting Lianghuai salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Governor-General Jiang Youjie had him restored to his former rank as acting Lianghuai salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鳳生以淮鹽極敝，條上十八事。

translations.literal: Fengsheng, seeing Huai salt utterly decayed, submitted eighteen proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Huai salt in utter ruin, Fengsheng submitted eighteen reform proposals.

sentences.zh: 攸銛採其議，改灶鹽，節浮費，濬河道，增屯船，緝場私、鄰私之出入，禁江船、漕船之夾帶，及清查庫款，督運淮北諸條，疏陳待施行，會詔捕鹽梟巨魁黃玉林，鳳生計招出首，責緝私贖罪。

translations.literal: Youjie adopted his plans, reformed stove salt, cut waste, dredged waterways, added transport boats, checked private salt at fields and borders, forbade smuggling on river and grain boats, and audited treasury funds and Huai north transport—memorialized for implementation—when an edict came to capture the great salt outlaw Huang Yulin; Fengsheng planned to induce accomplices, charge them to hunt smugglers and redeem guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Youjie adopted his plans—reforming stove salt, cutting waste, dredging channels, adding transport boats, sealing field and border smuggling, barring smuggling on river and grain boats, auditing treasury funds, and supervising Huai north transport—and memorialized them for action. When an edict ordered the capture of the great salt outlaw Huang Yulin, Fengsheng planned to turn accomplices, charging them to hunt smugglers in exchange for pardon.

sentences.zh: 攸銛已入告，旋因告訐置之獄，又得玉林所寄其黨私書，意反复，密疏請處以重法。

translations.literal: Youjie had already reported success, but then because of accusations put him in prison; he also received private letters Huang Yulin sent his gang, thought him fickle, and secretly memorialized for heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Youjie had already reported success, but then, after accusations, imprisoned him; he also received private letters Huang sent his gang, judged him treacherous, and secretly memorialized for severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 上以前後歧異，譴攸銛，鳳生亦降調。

translations.literal: The emperor, seeing the contradiction, rebuked Youjie and Fengsheng was also demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, seeing the contradiction, censured Youjie, and Fengsheng was demoted as well.

sentences.zh: 陶澍繼督兩江，與尚書王鼎、侍郎寶興會籌鹽法，合疏留鳳生襄議，於是大有興革，略與鳳生初議相出入；

translations.literal: Tao Shu succeeded as governor-general of the Two Jiangs; with Minister Wang Ding and Vice Minister Bao Xing he jointly planned salt law and together memorialized to retain Fengsheng to assist deliberation; great reforms followed, roughly agreeing with Fengsheng’s first proposals;
translations.idiomatic: Tao Shu became governor-general of the Two Jiangs and, with Minister Wang Ding and Vice Minister Bao Xing, jointly planned salt reform, memorializing together to keep Fengsheng in council. Major reforms followed, largely in line with his original proposals;

sentences.zh: 又奏以鳳生察湖廣銷引，勘議淮北改票事，鳳生雖去官，仍與鹽事終始。

translations.literal: they also memorialized Fengsheng to inspect Huguang sales and survey Huai north ticket reform; though Fengsheng had left office, he was still involved in salt affairs from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: they also had Fengsheng inspect Huguang sales and draft Huai north ticket reform. Though out of office, he remained bound up with salt policy from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 十二年，湖北大潦，總督盧坤疏留鳳生治江、漢堤工，袤亙數百里，半載告竣，秋水至，新堤有潰者，鳳生引咎乞疾歸。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Hubei flooded greatly; Governor Lu Kun memorialized to retain Fengsheng for Jiang and Han embankments spanning hundreds of li; in half a year work was reported finished; when autumn water came, new dikes burst in places; Fengsheng took blame and begged leave on illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Hubei flooded severely; Governor Lu Kun asked to retain Fengsheng for Jiang and Han dikes stretching hundreds of li. Half a year later the works were declared done, but when autumn floods came new dikes failed in places; Fengsheng accepted blame and pleaded illness to retire.

sentences.zh: 尋淮北票鹽大暢，陶澍以鳳生首議功上聞，促之出，未行而卒。

translations.literal: Soon Huai north ticket salt flourished greatly; Tao Shu reported Fengsheng’s leading merit to the throne and urged him out, but before he could go he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huai north ticket salt thrived; Tao Shu reported Fengsheng’s leading role to the throne and urged him back, but he died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 鳳生以仕為學，尤篤好圖誌，成浙西水利圖說備考、河北采風錄、江淮河運圖、漢江紀程、江漢宣防備考、淮南北場河運鹽走私道路圖，每吏一方，必能指畫其形勢，與所宜興革。

translations.literal: Fengsheng took office as study, especially loving maps and gazetteers, completing studies of western Zhejiang waterworks, Hebei investigations, Jiang-Huai river transport maps, Han River itineraries, Jiang-Han flood defense, and maps of Huai north and south salt smuggling routes; in every post he could sketch terrain and what should be reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Fengsheng treated office as scholarship and especially loved maps and gazetteers, producing studies of western Zhejiang hydraulics, Hebei field notes, Jiang-Huai transport charts, Han River itineraries, Jiang-Han flood defense, and smuggling routes on Huai north and south. In every post he could sketch the terrain and the reforms it needed.

sentences.zh: 四方大吏爭相疏調，少竟其用，惟治淮鹽尤為陶澍所倚藉焉。

translations.literal: Great officials everywhere competed to memorialize for his transfer, yet few could use him fully; only in Huai salt was he most relied on by Tao Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Officials across the empire fought to have him transferred, yet few could use him to the full; only in Huai salt was he most indispensable to Tao Shu.

sentences.zh: 黃冕，字服週，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: Huang Mian, courtesy name Fuzhou, was a native of Changsha, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Mian, whose courtesy name was Fuzhou, came from Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 年二十，官兩淮鹽大使，治淮、揚賑有聲。

translations.literal: At twenty he served as Lianghuai salt distribution commissioner and won renown for relief on the Huai and Yang regions.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he served as Lianghuai salt distribution commissioner and won renown for famine relief on the Huai and Yang regions.

sentences.zh: 初行海運，巡撫陶澍使赴上海集沙船與議，盡得要領，授江都知縣。

translations.literal: When sea transport first began, Governor Tao Shu sent him to Shanghai to gather sand boats for consultation; he mastered the essentials and was appointed magistrate of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: When sea transport was first launched, Governor Tao Shu sent him to Shanghai to gather sand-junk owners for consultation; mastering every detail, he was appointed magistrate of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 曆元和、上海，署太倉州，擢蘇州府同知，晉秩知府，署常州、鎮江，有大興作，大吏悉倚以辦。

translations.literal: He served Yuanhe and Shanghai, acted for Taicang subprefecture, was promoted subprefect of Suzhou prefecture and advanced to prefect, acting for Changzhou and Zhenjiang; when great works arose, high officials all relied on him to carry them out.
translations.idiomatic: He served Yuanhe and Shanghai, acted for Taicang, rose to Suzhou subprefect and then prefect, and acted for Changzhou and Zhenjiang; whenever major projects arose, senior officials relied on him to execute them.

sentences.zh: 疏治劉河海口，上海蒲匯塘，常州芙蓉江、孟河，冕皆躬任之。

translations.literal: Dredging the Liu River estuary, Shanghai’s Puhui Canal, Changzhou’s Furong River and Meng River—Mian personally took charge of each.
translations.idiomatic: Dredging the Liu River mouth, Shanghai’s Puhui Canal, Changzhou’s Furong River and Meng River—Mian took personal charge of each.

sentences.zh: 海疆兵事起，從總督裕謙赴浙江。

translations.literal: When coastal warfare began he followed Governor Yu Qian to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: When coastal war broke out he followed Governor Yu Qian to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 裕謙死難，冕牽連遣戍伊犁，既而林則徐亦至戍，議興屯田，冕佐治水利有功，赦還。

translations.literal: Yu Qian died in the crisis; Mian was implicated and sent to exile in Yili; soon Lin Zexu also arrived in exile; they planned to open military colonies; Mian assisted in waterworks with merit and was pardoned home.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian died in the crisis; Mian was implicated and exiled to Yili; soon Lin Zexu joined him there; they planned military colonies, and Mian’s work on irrigation won merit until he was pardoned home.

sentences.zh: 江蘇巡撫陸建瀛復調冕治海運，革漕費，歲省銀數十萬，為忌者所中，劾罷歸。

translations.literal: Jiangsu Governor Lu Jianying again called Mian to manage sea transport, reformed transport fees, saving hundreds of thousands of taels yearly; slandered by enemies, he was impeached and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu Governor Lu Jianying again summoned Mian to run sea transport, reformed transport fees, and saved hundreds of thousands of taels a year; enemies slandered him and he was impeached home.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，粵匪圍長沙，冕建守禦策。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng the Cantonese rebels besieged Changsha; Mian devised defense plans.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng, as Cantonese rebels besieged Changsha, Mian drafted defense plans.

sentences.zh: 及曾國籓治兵討賊，冕創釐稅，興茶鹽之利，軍餉取給焉。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan raised troops to suppress the rebels, Mian created the lijin tax and developed tea and salt profits, from which army funds were drawn.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan raised troops against the rebels, Mian created the lijin levy and developed tea and salt revenues that fed the army.

sentences.zh: 又開東征局，專餉曾國籓一軍。

translations.literal: He also opened the Eastern Expedition Bureau to supply only Zeng Guofan’s army.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened the Eastern Expedition Bureau devoted solely to provisioning Zeng Guofan’s force.

sentences.zh: 起授江西吉安知府，復以事劾免歸，仍以餉事自任，湘軍賴以成功。

translations.literal: Restored and appointed prefect of Ji’an in Jiangxi, again impeached and sent home, yet still took supply duties on himself; the Hunan army succeeded thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Restored to office as prefect of Ji’an in Jiangxi, he was again impeached home, yet still shouldered supply work on his own, and the Hunan army owed its success to that.

sentences.zh: 尋授雲南迤西道，辭病不赴，卒於家。

translations.literal: Soon appointed intendant of western Yunnan, he declined on illness and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon named intendant of western Yunnan, he declined on grounds of illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 冕仕宦初為陶澍、林則徐所知，晚在籍為駱秉章所倚任。

translations.literal: In office Mian was first known to Tao Shu and Lin Zexu; later at home he was relied on by Luo Bingzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In office Mian was first noticed by Tao Shu and Lin Zexu; later, living at home, he was entrusted by Luo Bingzhang.

sentences.zh: 時稱其幹濟，被謗亦甚云。

translations.literal: At the time he was called capable in practical affairs, though slandered greatly as well.
translations.idiomatic: People then praised his practical ability, though he was slandered just as fiercely.

sentences.zh: 俞德淵，字陶泉，甘肅平羅人。

translations.literal: Yu Deyuan, courtesy name Taoquan, was a native of Pingluo, Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Deyuan, whose courtesy name was Taoquan, came from Pingluo in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十二年進士，選庶吉士，散館授江蘇荊溪知縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi, was selected Hanlin bachelor, and on leaving the academy was appointed magistrate of Jingxi in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Jiaqing 22, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and on leaving the academy was appointed magistrate of Jingxi in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 始至，遮訴者百十輩，逾年，前訴者又易名來控，一見即識之，群驚為神。

translations.literal: On first arrival more than a hundred litigants blocked his way; after a year former complainants came again under other names; at one glance he recognized them and all marveled as at a god.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival more than a hundred litigants waylaid him; a year later the same complainants returned under new names, yet he recognized them at once and the crowd marveled as though he were divine.

sentences.zh: 調長洲，甚得民心。

translations.literal: Transferred to Changzhou, he won the people’s hearts deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Changzhou, he won the people’s deep affection.

sentences.zh: 遷蘇州督糧同知。

translations.literal: He was moved Suzhou grain transport subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Suzhou’s grain transport subprefect.

sentences.zh: 道光六年，初行海運，以德淵董其役，章程皆出手定，以憂去。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang sea transport first began; Deyuan directed the operation, every regulation drafted by his hand; he left on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 6 sea transport began; Deyuan directed it, drafting every regulation himself, then left on mourning.

sentences.zh: 八年，服闋，擢常州知府，調江寧。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, mourning ended, he was promoted prefect of Changzhou and transferred to Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when mourning ended, he was promoted prefect of Changzhou and transferred to Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 十年，宣宗以兩淮鹽法大壞，授陶澍為兩江總督，命尚書王鼎、侍郎寶興赴江南會議改革。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Xuanzong Emperor, seeing Lianghuai salt law utterly ruined, appointed Tao Shu governor-general of the Two Jiangs and ordered Minister Wang Ding and Vice Minister Bao Xing to Jiangnan to confer on reform.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, seeing Lianghuai salt law in ruins, the Xuanzong Emperor appointed Tao Shu governor-general of the Two Jiangs and sent Minister Wang Ding and Vice Minister Bao Xing to Jiangnan to plan reform.

sentences.zh: 時議者多主罷官商鹽，歸場灶科稅，以德淵有心計，使與議。

translations.literal: Most debaters urged abolishing merchant salt and returning tax to fields and stoves; because Deyuan had financial talent, he was made to join deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Most debaters wanted to abolish merchant salt and tax the fields and stoves instead; because Deyuan had a gift for accounts, he was brought into the talks.

sentences.zh: 德淵具議數千言，略謂：「鹽歸場灶，其法有三：一曰歸灶丁按䥕起科，然其中有難行者三：一在灶丁之逋欠，一在䥕鑊之私煎，一在災祲之藉口；

translations.literal: Deyuan drafted a memorial of several thousand words, roughly saying: “Returning salt to fields and stoves has three methods: first, tax stove households by cauldron—yet three difficulties: arrears of stove households, private boiling of cauldrons, and disaster as pretext;
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan drafted a memorial thousands of words long, arguing that returning salt to fields and stoves offered three approaches: first, tax stove households by cauldron—yet three difficulties: their arrears, private boiling, and pleas of disaster;

sentences.zh: 二曰歸場官給單收稅，難行者亦有三：一在額數之難定，一在稽查之難週，一在官吏之難恃；

translations.literal: second, field officials issue slips to collect tax—also three difficulties: hard to fix quotas, hard to inspect thoroughly, hard to rely on officials;
translations.idiomatic: second, field officials issue tax slips—again three difficulties: fixing quotas, thorough inspection, and trustworthy magistrates;

sentences.zh: 三曰歸場商認䥕納課，難行者亦有三：一在疲商之鑽充，一在殷戶之規避，一在垣外之私售。

translations.literal: third, field merchants acknowledge cauldrons and pay duty—also three difficulties: worn merchants filling posts, wealthy households evading duty, and private sales outside the yards.
translations.idiomatic: third, field merchants acknowledge cauldrons and pay duty—again three difficulties: depleted merchants buying posts, rich households evading tax, and private sales beyond the yards.

sentences.zh: 以上三法，共有九難。

translations.literal: Among the three methods there are nine difficulties in all.
translations.idiomatic: Across all three methods there are nine difficulties.

sentences.zh: 如就三者兼權之，則招商認䥕，猶為此善於彼。

translations.literal: If one weighs all three, recruiting merchants to acknowledge cauldrons is still better than the others.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing all three, recruiting merchants to acknowledge cauldrons is still the least bad.

sentences.zh: 苟得其人，或可講求盡善。

translations.literal: If the right man is found, perfection might be sought.
translations.idiomatic: With the right man in charge, one might even approach perfection.

sentences.zh: 顧事關圖始，果欲行之，則宜先定章程。

translations.literal: Yet this concerns founding a system; if it is truly to be done, regulations must first be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this is founding a system; if it is truly to be carried out, regulations must be settled first.

sentences.zh: 清灶僉商、改官易制諸事，非三年不能就緒。

translations.literal: Clearing stoves, enrolling merchants, changing official systems—these cannot be ready in less than three years.
translations.idiomatic: Clearing stoves, enrolling merchants, changing official systems—none can be ready in under three years.

sentences.zh: 此三年中，額課未可長懸也，場鹽未可停售也，各岸食鹽未可久缺也。

translations.literal: In those three years quotas cannot long hang in the air, field salt cannot stop selling, and every shore cannot long lack salt.
translations.idiomatic: During those three years quotas cannot hang in the air, field salt cannot cease sale, and every market cannot long go without salt.

sentences.zh: 新舊接替之時，非熟思審處，何能變通盡利乎？

translations.literal: At the juncture of old and new, without deep thought and careful handling, how can change bring full benefit?
translations.idiomatic: At the handoff from old to new, without deep thought and careful handling, how can reform yield full profit?

sentences.zh: 向來捆鹽之夫，淮北永豐有萬餘人，淮南老虎頸不下數万人，皆無賴遊民以此為事業。

translations.literal: Formerly the salt-bundling laborers—more than ten thousand at Yongfeng in Huai north, no fewer under Laohujing in Huai south—all were idle ruffians who made this their trade.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the salt-bundling gangs—more than ten thousand at Yongfeng in Huai north, no fewer under Tiger’s Neck in Huai south—were idle ruffians who lived by the trade.

sentences.zh: 一旦失所，此數万眾將安往？

translations.literal: Once they lose their livelihood, where will these tens of thousands go?
translations.idiomatic: Once they lose their livelihood, where will these tens of thousands go?

sentences.zh: 其患又不止私梟拒捕已也。

translations.literal: The harm is not only smugglers resisting arrest.
translations.idiomatic: The harm is not limited to smugglers resisting arrest.

sentences.zh: 」議上，陶澍深然之，乃與朝使定議，不歸場灶，仍用官商如故；

translations.literal: ” When the memorial went up, Tao Shu deeply approved; with the court envoys they fixed policy not to return to fields and stoves but keep merchant salt as before;
translations.idiomatic: ” When the memorial went up, Tao Shu strongly agreed; with the court envoys he fixed policy to keep merchant salt as before rather than return salt to fields and stoves;

sentences.zh: 惟奏罷鹽政，裁浮費，減窩價，凡積弊皆除之。

translations.literal: only memorialized to abolish the salt commissioner, cut waste, reduce nest prices, and remove every accumulated abuse.
translations.idiomatic: they only memorialized to abolish the salt commissioner, cut waste, lower nest prices, and purge every entrenched abuse.

sentences.zh: 薦德淵超擢兩淮鹽運使。

translations.literal: He recommended Deyuan for extraordinary promotion to Lianghuai salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Deyuan for extraordinary promotion to Lianghuai salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 德淵精會計，又知人善任。

translations.literal: Deyuan was skilled in accounts and good at employing men.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan excelled at accounts and knew how to employ the right men.

sentences.zh: 諸滯岸商憚往運，改以官督辦，千里行鹽，稽覈價用，瑣屑悉當。

translations.literal: Merchants on stagnant shores feared to transport; he changed to official supervision; transporting salt a thousand li, checking prices and costs, every detail was correct.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants on stagnant shores feared to transport; he shifted to official supervision; over a thousand li of transport he audited prices and costs until every detail was exact.

sentences.zh: 每運恆有餘利，盡以充庫，無私取。

translations.literal: Each transport often had surplus profit, all paid into the treasury, with no private taking.
translations.idiomatic: Each transport often yielded surplus, all paid into the treasury, never into private pockets.

sentences.zh: 兩淮本脂膏地，運使多以財結權貴及四方遊客，餘贍給寒畯，取聲譽，皆出商貲。

translations.literal: The Two Huai were a fat land; transport commissioners often used wealth to win powerful men and travelers everywhere, the rest given poor scholars for reputation—all from merchant money.
translations.idiomatic: The Two Huai were a rich province; transport commissioners often used wealth to court the powerful and travelers from every quarter, giving the rest to poor scholars for fame—all drawn from merchant funds.

sentences.zh: 德淵謹守筦鑰，失望者眾，言者時相攻訐，不顧也。

translations.literal: Deyuan strictly guarded the keys; many were disappointed; critics often attacked him, yet he paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan guarded the treasury keys strictly; many were disappointed; critics attacked him constantly, yet he paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 在任五年，力崇節儉，妻子常衣布素，揚州華侈之俗為之一變。

translations.literal: In five years in office he strongly promoted frugality; wife and children always wore plain cloth; Yangzhou’s luxurious ways changed because of him.
translations.idiomatic: In five years he championed frugality; wife and children wore only plain cloth; Yangzhou’s extravagant customs shifted because of him.

sentences.zh: 尚書黃鉞子中民為場大使，欲得美職，德淵曰：「美職以待有功，中民無功不可得。

translations.literal: Minister Huang Yue’s son Zhongmin was a field commissioner wanting a fine post; Deyuan said: “Fine posts await merit; Zhongmin has no merit and cannot have one.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Huang Yue’s son Zhongmin was a field commissioner seeking a prized post; Deyuan said, “Prized posts await merit; Zhongmin has none and cannot have one.”

sentences.zh: 」堅不與。

translations.literal: ” He firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 陶澍益賢之，薦其才可大用，以循良久在鹽官可惜，上亦嘉之，未及擢用而卒。

translations.literal: Tao Shu esteemed him more, recommended his talent for great use; because he had long followed rules in salt office it was a pity, the emperor also praised him, but before promotion he died.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Shu esteemed him further and recommended him for high office; because he had long served salt posts by the book it was a pity; the emperor praised him too, but he died before promotion.

sentences.zh: 姚瑩，字石甫，安徽桐城人。

translations.literal: Yao Ying, courtesy name Shifu, was a native of Tongcheng, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Ying, whose courtesy name was Shifu, came from Tongcheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年進士，授福建平和知縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi and was appointed magistrate of Pinghe in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Jiaqing 13 and was appointed magistrate of Pinghe in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 調龍溪，俗健悍，械鬥仇殺無虛日。

translations.literal: Transferred to Longxi, where the custom was fierce and armed fights and vendetta killings occurred daily without pause.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Longxi, where the people were fierce and armed brawls and vendetta killings happened almost daily.

sentences.zh: 瑩擒巨惡立斃之，收豪猾為用，予以自新。

translations.literal: Ying seized great villains and executed them on the spot, took powerful scoundrels into service and gave them a chance to reform.
translations.idiomatic: Ying seized great villains and executed them at once, enlisted powerful scoundrels and gave them a chance to reform.

sentences.zh: 親巡問疾苦，使侵奪者各還舊業，誓解仇讎。

translations.literal: He personally toured to ask their hardships, made aggressors return old holdings, and made them swear to end vendettas.
translations.idiomatic: He toured in person to hear their hardships, made aggressors return seized property, and had them swear to end blood feuds.

sentences.zh: 擇強力者為家長，約束族眾，籍壯丁為鄉勇，逐捕盜賊，有犯，責家長縛送。

translations.literal: He chose strong men as household heads to restrain clans, registered able-bodied men as village militia, hunted bandits, and when crimes occurred held household heads responsible to bind and deliver offenders.
translations.idiomatic: He chose strong men as household heads to restrain their clans, registered able-bodied men as village militia, hunted bandits, and when crimes occurred held heads responsible to seize and deliver the culprits.

sentences.zh: 械鬥平，盜賊亦戢，治行為閩中第一。

translations.literal: Armed fights ceased and bandits were curbed; his governance ranked first in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Armed brawls ceased and bandits were curbed; his record ranked first in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 調台灣，署海防同知、噶瑪蘭同知，坐事落職。

translations.literal: Transferred to Taiwan, he acted coastal defense subprefect and Gamlan subprefect, was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Taiwan, he acted coastal defense subprefect and Gamlan subprefect, then was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋以噶瑪蘭獲盜功，复官。

translations.literal: Soon because of merit capturing bandits at Gamlan he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for capturing bandits at Gamlan, he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸，服闋，改發江蘇，歷金壇、元和、武進。

translations.literal: He returned on his father’s mourning; when mourning ended he was reassigned to Jiangsu, serving Jintan, Yuanhe, and Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for his father’s mourning; when it ended he was reassigned to Jiangsu, serving Jintan, Yuanhe, and Wujin.

sentences.zh: 遷高郵知州，擢兩淮監掣同知，護鹽運使。

translations.literal: He was moved prefect of Gaoyou, promoted Lianghuai transport control subprefect, and protected the salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Gaoyou prefect, promoted Lianghuai transport control subprefect, and protected the salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先後疆吏趙慎畛、陶澍、林則徐皆薦其可大用。

translations.literal: Border officials Zhao Shenzhe, Tao Shu, and Lin Zexu all recommended him for great appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials Zhao Shenzhe, Tao Shu, and Lin Zexu all recommended him for high office.

sentences.zh: 道光十年，特擢台灣道。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Daoguang he was specially promoted Taiwan intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 10 he was specially promoted Taiwan intendant.

sentences.zh: 及海疆戒嚴，瑩與總兵達洪阿預為戰守計。

translations.literal: When the coast was placed on alert, Ying and Regional Commander Da Hong’a prepared plans of war and defense in advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the coast was placed on alert, Ying and Regional Commander Da Hong’a prepared war and defense plans in advance.

sentences.zh: 達洪阿性剛，與同官鮮合，瑩推誠相接，一日謁謝曰：「武人不學，為子所容久矣，自今聽子而行。

translations.literal: Da Hong’a was stubborn and rarely agreed with fellow officials; Ying treated him sincerely; one day Da came to thank him, saying: “A martial man unlearned—I have long been tolerated by you; from today I heed you.
translations.idiomatic: Da Hong’a was stubborn and rarely got on with colleagues; Ying treated him sincerely; one day Da came to thank him, saying, “I am an unlettered soldier—you have borne with me long; from today I follow your lead.”

sentences.zh: 」二十一年秋，英兵兩犯雞籠海口，明年正月，又犯大安港。

translations.literal: ” In autumn of the twenty-first year British troops twice attacked Keelung harbor; in the first month of the next year they attacked Da’an harbor again.
translations.idiomatic: ” In autumn of the twenty-first year British troops twice attacked Keelung; in the first month of the next year they attacked Da’an harbor again.

sentences.zh: 瑩設方略，與達洪阿督兵連卻之，大有斬獲，收前所失寧波、廈門砲械甚多。

translations.literal: Ying devised strategy; with Da Hong’a he directed troops to repel them repeatedly with great kills and captures, recovering much artillery lost earlier at Ningbo and Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Ying devised strategy; with Da Hong’a he directed troops to repel them again and again with heavy kills and captures, recovering much artillery lost earlier at Ningbo and Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 敵構奸民煽亂，海寇亦竊發，皆即捕戮，一方屹然，詔嘉獎，加二品銜，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: The enemy incited traitors to stir rebellion and sea bandits also rose; all were quickly captured and executed; the region stood firm; the throne praised and rewarded him, adding second-rank rank and a hereditary yunqiwei.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy incited traitors and sea bandits also rose; all were swiftly captured and executed; the region held firm; the court praised and rewarded him, adding second-rank rank and a hereditary yunqiwei.

sentences.zh: 洎江寧議款求息事，遂有台灣鎮道冒功之獄。

translations.literal: When peace was negotiated at Jiangning to end the affair, there arose the case of Taiwan commander and intendant claiming merit falsely.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was negotiated at Jiangning to end the war, a case arose over the Taiwan commander and intendant falsely claiming merit.

sentences.zh: 故事，台灣以懸隔海外，加兵備道按察使銜，得與鎮臣專奏事。

translations.literal: By precedent Taiwan, being isolated overseas, gave the military intendant the provincial judicial commissioner rank so he and the commander could memorialize separately.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, because Taiwan lay isolated overseas, the military intendant bore the provincial judicial commissioner rank so he and the regional commander could memorialize on their own.

sentences.zh: 雞籠、大安之捷，飛章入告，總督怡良心不平。

translations.literal: Victories at Keelung and Da’an were reported by urgent memorial; Governor Yi Liang was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Victories at Keelung and Da’an were reported by urgent memorial, to Governor Yi Liang’s displeasure.

sentences.zh: 英兵留駐鼓浪嶼，前獲俘欲解內地，勢不能達，奏請便宜誅之，以絕內患，已報可，怡良仍令解省。

translations.literal: British troops remained on Gulangyu; captives taken earlier could not be sent inland; memorial asked for summary execution to end internal trouble—already approved—yet Yi Liang still ordered them sent to the province.
translations.idiomatic: British troops remained on Gulangyu; earlier captives could not be sent inland; a memorial asked leave to execute them summarily to end internal trouble and was approved, yet Yi Liang still ordered them sent to the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 瑩與達洪阿謀曰：「大府意欲市德，藉以退鼓浪嶼之兵。

translations.literal: Ying and Da Hong’a discussed: “The grand coordinator wishes to curry favor and use this to withdraw troops from Gulangyu.
translations.idiomatic: Ying and Da Hong’a discussed: “The governor intends to curry favor and use the prisoners to withdraw troops from Gulangyu.

sentences.zh: 兵不可退，徒示弱，不如殺之！

translations.literal: Troops cannot withdraw—that only shows weakness; better kill them!
translations.idiomatic: Troops must not withdraw—that only shows weakness; better kill them!”

sentences.zh: 」怡良愈怒，諸帥並忌之。

translations.literal: Yi Liang grew angrier and commanders all resented them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Liang grew angrier, and the commanders all resented them.

sentences.zh: 款議既成，交還敵俘，以妄殺被劾，逮問。

translations.literal: After peace was made, captives were handed back; for wrongful killing they were impeached and arrested for trial.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made the captives were handed back; for wrongful killing they were impeached and brought to trial.

sentences.zh: 瑩與達洪阿約，義不與俘虜質，即自引咎。

translations.literal: Ying and Da Hong’a agreed they would not bargain with captives and took blame themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Ying and Da Hong’a agreed they would not trade on captives and took the blame themselves.

sentences.zh: 宣宗心知台灣功，入獄六日，特旨以同知直隸州知州發往四川效用，至則復為總督寶興所忌。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor knew Taiwan’s merit at heart; after six days in prison a special edict sent him as Tongzhou subprefect in Zhili to serve in Sichuan; on arrival he was again resented by Governor Bao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzong Emperor knew Taiwan’s merit at heart; after six days in prison a special edict sent him as Tongzhou subprefect in Zhili to serve in Sichuan; on arrival Governor Bao Xing resented him again.

sentences.zh: 會西藏兩呼圖克圖相爭，檄往平之。

translations.literal: When two Hutuktus of Tibet quarreled, an order went to go pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When two Tibetan Hutuktus quarreled, he was ordered to go pacify them.

sentences.zh: 瑩謂：「夷人難以德化。

translations.literal: Ying said: “Barbarians are hard to civilize by virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Ying said, “Barbarians are hard to civilize by virtue alone.

sentences.zh: 失職下僚，孑身往，徒損國威。

translations.literal: A dismissed subordinate going alone only harms national prestige.
translations.idiomatic: A dismissed subordinate going alone will only harm national prestige.”

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: They did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: They did not listen.

sentences.zh: 及至乍雅，果不得要領而返。

translations.literal: When he reached Zhaya he indeed gained no key points and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Zhaya he indeed gained no leverage and returned.

sentences.zh: 總督劾其畏難規避，責再往。

translations.literal: The governor impeached him for shirking difficulty and evading duty and ordered him to go again.
translations.idiomatic: The governor impeached him for shirking difficulty and ordered him back.

sentences.zh: 事竣，補蓬州。

translations.literal: When the affair ended he was appointed Pengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair ended he was appointed magistrate of Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 在州二年，引疾歸。

translations.literal: In the prefecture two years he cited illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in the prefecture he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，黜大學士穆彰阿，詔宣示中外，並及瑩與達洪阿被陷狀，於是復起用，授湖北武昌鹽法道，未行，擢廣西按察使，命參大學士賽尚阿軍事。

translations.literal: When the Wenzong Emperor ascended, Grand Secretary Mu Zhang’a was dismissed; an edict announced to all within and without, including the situation in which Ying and Da Hong’a had been framed; he was then restored, appointed Hubei Wuchang salt law intendant; before he could go he was promoted Guangxi provincial judicial commissioner and ordered to join Grand Secretary Sai Shang’a’s military staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wenzong Emperor ascended, Grand Secretary Mu Zhang’a was dismissed; an edict announced the case at home and abroad, including how Ying and Da Hong’a had been framed; he was restored, named Hubei Wuchang salt law intendant; before he could depart he was promoted Guangxi provincial judicial commissioner and ordered onto Grand Secretary Sai Shang’a’s staff.

sentences.zh: 時廣西寇漸熾，諸將不合，師久無功。

translations.literal: At the time Guangxi bandits grew fierce; generals did not cooperate; the army long had no success.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi bandits were then growing fierce; generals would not cooperate; the campaign long lacked success.

sentences.zh: 瑩至，任為翼長。

translations.literal: When Ying arrived he was made wing commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying arrived he was made wing commander.

sentences.zh: 大軍圍賊紫金山，瑩言流賊如水，必環攻以斷其逸，不聽，賊遂竄永安。

translations.literal: The main army besieged the bandits on Purple Gold Mountain; Ying said roaming bandits are like water and must be encircled to cut escape; they did not listen and the bandits fled to Yong’an.
translations.idiomatic: The main army besieged the bandits on Purple Gold Mountain; Ying said roaming bandits are like water and must be fully encircled to cut escape; they refused, and the bandits fled to Yong’an.

sentences.zh: 又上書請斬僨事將，復不聽。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to execute the blundering general; again they did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to execute the blundering general; again they refused.

sentences.zh: 永安城小，都統烏蘭泰軍西南，提督向榮軍東北，合滇、黔、楚、蜀兵四萬餘人，賊數千壁險死鬥。

translations.literal: Yong’an city was small; Commandant Ulan Tai’s army was southwest, Regional Commander Xiang Rong’s northeast; together Yunnan, Guizhou, Huguang, and Sichuan troops exceeded forty thousand; several thousand bandits held peril and fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Yong’an was a small city; Commandant Ulan Tai’s force lay southwest, Regional Commander Xiang Rong’s northeast; together troops from Yunnan, Guizhou, Huguang, and Sichuan exceeded forty thousand, while several thousand bandits held the heights and fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 水竇者，永安東北之隘也，緣山徑可達桂林。

translations.literal: Shuidou was the pass northeast of Yong’an; a mountain path along it could reach Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Shuidou was the pass northeast of Yong’an; a mountain path there could reach Guilin.

sentences.zh: 瑩與烏蘭泰皆主擊水竇，絕賊外援，向榮不從，自由龍寮嶺進而敗，乃議開水竇一路縱賊逸，尾追擊之。

translations.literal: Ying and Ulan Tai both urged striking Shuidou to cut bandit aid; Xiang Rong refused and advanced by Longliao Ridge instead and was defeated; then they debated opening Shuidou to let bandits escape and pursuing from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Ying and Ulan Tai both urged striking Shuidou to cut outside aid; Xiang Rong refused, advanced by Longliao Ridge, and was defeated; then they debated opening Shuidou to let the bandits out and pursue from behind.

sentences.zh: 瑩力辯其失，賽尚阿仍用向榮策，賊果突圍出犯桂林，烏蘭泰戰死，賽尚阿逮問。

translations.literal: Ying strongly argued the error; Sai Shang’a still used Xiang Rong’s plan; bandits broke out and struck Guilin; Ulan Tai died in battle; Sai Shang’a was arrested for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Ying argued fiercely against the error; Sai Shang’a still followed Xiang Rong’s plan; the bandits broke out, struck Guilin, Ulan Tai died in battle, and Sai Shang’a was arrested for trial.

sentences.zh: 賊勢益熾，連陷興安、全州，犯湖南，遂不可製。

translations.literal: Bandit power grew fiercer, successively taking Xing’an and Quanzhou, invading Hunan, and then could not be controlled.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit power swelled, successively taking Xing’an and Quanzhou, invading Hunan, until the situation was beyond control.

sentences.zh: 瑩隨軍至湖南，巡撫張亮基奏署按察使，憂憤致疾，卒於官。

translations.literal: Ying followed the army to Hunan; Governor Zhang Liangji memorialized him acting provincial judicial commissioner; grief and anger brought illness and he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Ying followed the army into Hunan; Governor Zhang Liangji memorialized him acting provincial judicial commissioner; grief and anger brought illness and he died in office.

sentences.zh: 瑩師事從祖鼐，不好經生章句，務通大意，見諸施行。

translations.literal: Ying studied under his grand-uncle Nai, disliked classical pedantry, sought to grasp the main idea and apply it in action.
translations.idiomatic: Ying studied under his grand-uncle Yao Nai, disliked classical pedantry, and sought the main idea he could put into practice.

sentences.zh: 文章善持論，指陳時事利害，慷慨深切。

translations.literal: His essays argued well, pointing out current benefits and harms with passionate depth.
translations.idiomatic: His essays argued forcefully, laying out the gains and losses of the age with passionate depth.

sentences.zh: 所著東溟文集、奏稿、後湘詩集、東槎紀略、康輶紀行及雜著諸書，為中復堂全集，行於世。

translations.literal: His works Collected Writings from the Eastern Sea, Memorials, Later Xiang Poetry, Notes from the Eastern Raft, Record of the Imperial Journey, and other books, collected as the Complete Works of the Zhongfu Hall, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Collected Writings from the Eastern Sea, Memorials, Later Xiang Poetry, Notes from the Eastern Raft, Record of the Imperial Journey, and other works, gathered as the Complete Works of the Zhongfu Hall, circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子濬昌，能繼家學。

translations.literal: His son Junchang could continue the family learning.
translations.idiomatic: His son Junchang continued the family scholarship.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓以名家子留佐幕，官江西安福、湖北竹山知縣。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan kept him as a staff member as a son of a famous house; he served as magistrate of Anfu in Jiangxi and Zhushan in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan kept him on staff as the son of a noted house; he served as magistrate of Anfu in Jiangxi and Zhushan in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 工詩，有五瑞堂集。

translations.literal: Skilled in poetry, he had the Five Auspices Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote poetry well and left the Five Auspices Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 論曰：林培厚救荒治河有實績，而以察吏招忌。

translations.literal: The judgment says: Lin Peihou had real achievement in famine relief and river works, yet drew resentment by inspecting officials.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Lin Peihou achieved real results in famine relief and river works, yet drew resentment by inspecting subordinates.

sentences.zh: 李宗傳便宜平夷，功在邊方。

translations.literal: Li Zongchuan conveniently pacified the Yi with merit on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongchuan pacified the Yi on the frontier by expedient means with lasting merit.

sentences.zh: 王鳳生、俞德淵佐陶澍治淮鹽，尤濟時之才。

translations.literal: Wang Fengsheng and Yu Deyuan assisted Tao Shu in governing Huai salt and were especially talents for the age.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fengsheng and Yu Deyuan assisted Tao Shu in governing Huai salt and were especially the kind of talent the times needed.

sentences.zh: 姚瑩保岩疆，挫強敵，反遭讒譴，然朝廷未嘗不諒其忠勤，海內引領望其再用，亦不可謂不遇矣。

translations.literal: Yao Ying defended the coast, checked a strong enemy, yet suffered slander and punishment; yet the court never failed to appreciate his loyal diligence; the realm looked to his reuse—he cannot be called ill-favored.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Ying defended the coast, blunted a strong enemy, yet suffered slander and punishment; still the court never failed to value his loyal service, and the realm looked to his return—he can hardly be called ill-used.
